- `AWS Cloud Provider attempts to delete LoadBalancer security group it didn’t provision`
- `AWS Cloud Provider creates default LoadBalancer security group even if annotation [service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups] is present`

How is this related to #77557 which is related to "AWS not updating security group for loadBalancerSourceRanges"

And did you address @M00nF1sh 's comment?

@leakingtapan ,

I have updated the Issue Number.

I need to add more code in create step to not create SG when this annotation [service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups] is present .

Regards
Bhagwat

## Below is my proposal on this issue which does not solve the problem 100% but tries to fix major problems.
## Problems:
- Even if we have the annotation  `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups` we are creating a new security group.
- We are trying to delete the Security groups provided with annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups` which has not been created by k8s system.

## Solution :

- Stop creating new Security group for load balancer if customers are using annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups`.
- Allow deletion of Security group which has been created previously. May be we can stop deleting from next k8s version.
- Fileter out annotated SG from selection list to not call deletion on the SG not created by k8s system.


This solution does not solve the edge triggered problem but minimizes the impact.

- Customers will not hit the SG limit and API throttling.
- New clusters created would not see the deletion failure if its not edge triggered.


if we are OK with this proposal I can go ahead and make the change and update the PR.

@wongma7 @leakingtapan @micahhausler @M00nF1sh and @jsafrane 

Regards
Bhagwat

> Filter out annotated SG from selection list to not call deletion on the SG not created by k8s system.

This basically means "every SG not specified in the annotation is provisioned by K8s"
Suppose an user create an Service with annotation `SG1`, and an operator manually added `SG2` to that ELB, that SG2 will be deleted when deleting Service.

Instead, I think we should use a way to identify the securityGroups provisioned by K8s directly(e.g. through name or tag).

@M00nF1sh ,

I liked the idea 
`Instead,I think we should use a way to identify the securityGroups provisioned by K8s directly(e.g. through name or tag)` 
but in this case as well there would be a problem where if user adds the same name tag then we will be trying to delete.

but once we make the upstream doc with clear understanding about this tag then it will be much  better.


I can go with this approach , but for being backward compatible we still need to allow delete the tags which we are using Today or clusterId as tag.

> Instead,I think we should use a way to identify the securityGroups provisioned by K8s directly(e.g. through name or tag)

This was already added by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74311 .

The absence of a cluster tag like `kubernetes.io/cluster/<ClusterID>` on the SG is supposed to mean the SG is ignored and not deleted.

So I am curious how come it doesn't seem to work for the SGs specified in service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups.

Added code to perform following :

- Stop creating new Security group for load balancer if customers are using annotation service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups.
- Allow deletion of Security group which has been created previously. May be we can stop deleting from next k8s version.
- Fileter out annotated SG from selection list to not call deletion on the SG not created by k8s system.

issue_context.title: AWS Cloud Provider attempts to delete LoadBalancer security group it didn’t provision
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

- Created multiple services with LoadBalancerType as ELB , added a annotation of  `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups` with the same SG for all services. 
- Deleted one of the services.
- The cloudcontroller tries to delete the SG by annotation. 
- This also causing aws api throttling. 

**What you expected to happen**:

- Service and ELB should get deleted but not the non provisioned SG.


**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

See above...

**Anything else we need to know?**:

It get introduced in the PR #62774

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.13 and above
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:AWS
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
